2. This appeal has been filed on behalf of the appellant under Section 374(2) read with Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 against the judgment of conviction dated 12.10.2023 and the order of sentence dated 19.10.2023 rendered by the learned Additional Sessions Judge- VI-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Patna in Special POCSO Case No. 86 of 2021 arising out of Jakkanpur P.S. Case No. 262 of Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: 3. The appeal has been admitted and, for the present, the appellant prays for grant of bail and for suspension of sentence imposed by the learned trial court till final disposal of the appeal.
4. Learned Senior Advocate for the appellant has supplied the copy of the deposition of the prosecution witnesses.
Learned Senior Advocate referred the same and thereafter submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove with regard to the age of the victim and there is no age determination of the victim.
It is further submitted that the Investigating Agency did not collect any documentary evidence i.e., the Birth Certificate or the school register of the victim.

It is further submitted that in absence of any finding with regard to the fact that the victim was minor on the date of occurrence,
conviction cannot be Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.31 of 2024(12) dt.10-12-2024 recorded under the provisions of POCSO Act.

5. Learned Senior Advocate would thereafter contend that even from the deposition given by PW-1,
the doctor, who had examined the victim, it is revealed that the PW-1 has specifically admitted during cross-examination that it is difficult to say whether forceful sex was committed with the victim or not as there was no sign of forceful sex on the victim.

Learned Senior Advocate, therefore,
contended that medical evidence does not support the version of the victim.

6. Learned Senior Advocate would thereafter submit that there are major contradictions and inconsistencies in the deposition of the prosecution witnesses with regard to the manner of occurrence and the place of occurrence.

It is contended that the informant, who is mother of the victim, had given the written complaint wherein she had stated that she came to know about the incident when she returned to the house at about 6:00 PM and the place of occurrence was shown as her room.

However, from the deposition given by PW-6, it would reveal that the victim called the said witness on his mobile phone and when PW-6 came to the house of the victim, he found that the victim was unconscious and, therefore, she was taken to the police station.
However, it has been pointed out by Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.31 of 2024(12) dt.10-12-2024 learned Senior Advocate from deposition, more particularly, paragraph-14 of cross-examination of PW-3, the mother of the victim, that when she came to the place of occurrence and came to know about the incident, she took her daughter to the police station, at that time, she along with her husband,
another daughter and victim were present, none else was present in the police station.
It is also contended that even PW-3 (mother) has deposed before the Court that when the victim had gone on the terrace, the incident took place.

Learned Senior Advocate, therefore, urged that the present is the case of false implication wherein, the appellant, who is aged about 62, years has been falsely implicated because of the dispute between the neighbours.

Learned Senior Advocate, therefore,
urged that appellant be released on bail and the sentence imposed by the learned trial court be suspended.

7. On the other hand, learned APP for the Respondent- State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail by contending that from the evidence led by the prosecution, it is revealed that victim was minor on Ram Vinay Prasad Gupta vs The State Of Bihar on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69229439/
2 the date of occurrence and merely because there are minor contradictions and discrepancies in the deposition of the prosecution witnesses, the case of the prosecution may not be discarded at this stage.

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P. Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.31 of 2024(12) dt.10-12-2024 would further submit that the prosecution had examined the witnesses from which it is prima facie revealed that the appellant has committed rape on the minor girl aged about 12 years and looking to the seriousness of the incident in question and the allegations levelled against the appellant herein

,
he may not be released on bail as prayed for by learned Senior Advocate for the appellant.
8. We have considered the submissions canvassed by the learned Advocates appearing for the parties.
We have also perused the deposition of the prosecution witnesses and the trial court records.

Prima facie, it would reveal that the mother of the victim had given the written complaint,
wherein she had specifically stated that the incident took place at about 11:00 AM on 16.06.2021 in her room and when she returned to her house at about 06:00 PM, her daughter i.e., the victim,
narrated about the incident and, therefore, they have gone to the police station, where the written complaint was given.
It would further reveal from the deposition of PW-3 (informant), who is mother of the victim, that the incident took place on the terrace.
However, the victim (PW-4) has deposed before the Court that the incident took place in the room near to the terrace.
Thus, prima facie, there is discrepancy with regard to the place of Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.31 of 2024(12) dt.10-12-2024 occurrence

. Now, it is further revealed from the deposition of PW-6, who is projected as independent witness by the prosecution, that the victim called him on his mobile phone at about 01:00 PM and informed him that rape has been committed on her, therefore, he immediately went to the house of the victim.
Victim was unconscious at that point of time and thereafter she was taken to the police station where she regained consciousness.

However, at this stage, if the deposition given by PW-3 (informant), who is mother of the victim, is carefully examined, it is revealed that the said witness has admitted during cross-examination in paragraph-14 that when she reached to the place of occurrence, i.e., her house, she came to know that rape has been committed on her daughter and, therefore, she along with her husband, another daughter and victim went to the police station and except them none else was present at the police station.
9. Thus, prima facie, learned Senior Advocate is right in submitting that different story has been projected by the prosecution with regard to the place of occurrence and the manner of occurrence.
10. Even from the deposition given by PW-1, the doctor, who had examined the victim, it would reveal that the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.31 of 2024(12) dt.10-12-2024
said witness has admitted during cross-examination that it is difficult to say whether forceful sex has been committed with the victim or not.
The said witness has further admitted that there is no sign of man discharge on the general part of the victim and during the medical examination, the vagina of victim was found to be intact.
11. From the aforesaid deposition of the doctor, prima facie, we are of the view that medical evidence does not support the version of the prosecution.

sentences.text: 12. From the deposition given by PW-2, the Investigating Officer, it is revealed that the Investigating Officer has not made any effort by collecting the documentary evidence with regard to the age of the victim.
The prosecution has failed to produce any Birth Certificate, Aadhar Card or any school register before the trial court.
13. By examining PW-1, the doctor, the prosecution has tried to point out that the age of victim is between 10-12 years.

However, no specific finding has been recorded by the trial court by determining the age of the victim as per the procedure prescribed under Section 94 of Juvenile Justice Act and the Rules framed thereunder.

14. Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.31 of 2024(12) dt.10-12-2024 of the present case coupled with the specific contention raised by the learned Senior Advocate for the appellant that the appellant is aged about 60 years and the said aspect has been admitted by the prosecution witnesses and with regard to the suggestion put to the prosecution witnesses coupled with the examination of the defense witnesses, the theory of false implication has been projected by the defence, we are of the view that the present is a case where prima facie false implication cannot be ruled out.

15. Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the present case, we are of the view that the prayer made by the appellant for grant of bail and for suspension of sentence deserves consideration.

16. Accordingly, appellant is ordered to be released on bail during pendency of the present appeal on executing bond of Rs. 15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand) and upon furnishing two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Patna in Special POCSO Case No. 86 of 2021 arising out of Jakkanpur P.S. Case No. 262 of 2021 and the sentence imposed by the trial court is suspended so far as this appellant is concerned.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.31 of 2024(12) dt.10-12-2024 17.
It is clarified that the aforesaid observations are tentative observations made by this Court while considering the request of the appellant for grant of bail.
18. The appellant should co-operate in this court till disposal of the appeal.
19. Realisation of fine shall also remain stayed during the pendency of this appeal.

(Vipul M. Pancholi, J) ( Dr. Anshuman, J) GKS/-
